Given a tool whose spec has env: {"API_KEY": ...} and a secret reference in its config, When a sharee reads it, Then the response contains no env key and no secret reference string.
Given a tool shared without expose_spec, When a sharee calls host.tool_spec_shared, Then the response is spec_not_exposed naming <owner_ns>.<name>.
Given a tool not shared with the caller, When it calls host.tool_spec_shared, Then the response is the same not-found shape host.tool_call returns for an unshared tool.

Given a 64 KiB spec, When 50 sharees read it concurrently, Then p95 < 100 ms and every response is identical.
Given three reads by sharees, When the owner lists tools, Then the row shows spec_reads: 3 and an exposed_at timestamp.

Given prod mcphost after deploy, When tenant A publishes a python tool with one env entry and shares it to a group containing tenant B with expose_spec: true, and tenant B calls host.tool_spec_shared, Then B receives the source and no env, and A's host.calls.list shows B's read (Live).

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a sharee need to read a shared tool's spec at all, rather than just calling it?
five_whys_trace.a: Problem statement: the compete tournament's round-two builders are told to fork round-one winners, but 'fork' has no mechanism today -- tool_list never returns spec, and a sharee's only surface is host.tool_call. Without a read path, the tournament cannot measure recombination and the product's agent-to-agent story stops at calling, never at building on.

five_whys_trace.q: Why an owner opt-in flag (expose_spec, default closed) rather than exposing spec automatically to every sharee?
five_whys_trace.a: Goals: 'Owner opt-in per share, default closed.' A share today only grants call access; automatically also granting read access would be a silent behavior change for every tool an owner has already shared, and a tool wrapping a paid/rate-limited upstream (the share-a-tool-not-a-key pattern) is exactly the kind of tool an owner would NOT want forked sight-unseen by every group member.

five_whys_trace.q: Why redact env and secret references even when the owner has explicitly opted into exposure, rather than trusting expose_spec: true to mean 'show everything'?
five_whys_trace.a: Goals: 'env and secret references never leave the owner's tenant' -- User story 2: even with expose_spec: true, a sharee sees the source and env variable NAMES but never values or secret refs. Exposing the spec's shape (so a sharee can fork the logic) and exposing the owner's credentials are two different decisions; this PRD only ever makes the first one available, never the second, regardless of the flag.

five_whys_trace.q: Why must a not-shared tool and a shared-but-unexposed tool return two different refusal shapes (ToolNotFound vs spec_not_exposed) rather than one generic refusal?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 4/User story 3: a sharee shared without exposure should get a refusal that SAYS the owner has not exposed it, not a not-found -- useful signal to ask the owner to flip the flag. A tool never shared with the caller must stay indistinguishable from one that doesn't exist at all (the same 'never leak that the tool exists' invariant call_shared_tool already enforces), so collapsing both into one shape would either leak existence or hide the useful spec_not_exposed signal.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does host.tool_spec_shared need its own p95<100ms budget under 50 concurrent readers (AC8) rather than inheriting whatever host.tool_call's cross-tenant path already tolerates?
five_whys_trace.a: Non-functional: 'p95 for host.tool_spec_shared under 100 ms for a 64 KiB spec' -- User story 5/PRD Success metrics: the compete round's builders are expected to read a winner's spec in bulk right after a round closes, a genuinely concurrent read pattern host.tool_call's per-call sandbox dispatch was never measured against; a slow read path here would bottleneck the tournament's own round-two kickoff, not just one caller's own latency.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Should a tenant's clients: allowlist/approve decision be enforced at GET /oauth/authorize (before any tenant is known) or only once tenant ownership is proven at the consent POST?
